Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
What is the payment received for the use of capital?

options.A: interest
options.B: profit
options.C: rent
options.D: wage

questions.questionText: Which type of good would be over-consumed because of information failure?

options.A: demerit
options.B: inferior
options.C: merit
options.D: public

questions.questionText: What does the phrase ‘ceteris paribus’ mean?

options.A: All the resources used are of equal quality.
options.B: Everything else remains unchanged.
options.C: The price mechanism rations scarce goods.
options.D: The variable under consideration is held constant.

questions.questionText: What could explain a shift of an upward-sloping supply curve to the right?

options.A: an increase in firms’ unit labour costs
options.B: an increase in the number of firms in the industry
options.C: an increase in the price of the good
options.D: an indirect tax imposed on the good

questions.questionText: When will it not be possible to use price as a rationing mechanism?

options.A: when a good has a number of close substitutes
options.B: when a good is an inferior good
options.C: when the demand for a good is perfectly inelastic
options.D: when the quantity of a good is in fixed supply

questions.questionText: What is necessary for demand for a good to be effective?

options.A: The consumer must have the ability to buy the product.
options.B: The consumer must receive consumer surplus.
options.C: The good must be sold in the private sector of the economy.
options.D: There must be a successful advertising campaign.

questions.questionText: Why is the price elasticity of demand for a particular brand of coffee likely to be higher than the price elasticity of demand for coffee in general?

options.A: Coffee in general takes up a higher proportion of consumers’ income.
options.B: Consumers may be very loyal to a particular brand of coffee.
options.C: There are more substitutes for a particular brand of coffee than for coffee in general.
options.D: Total demand for coffee is higher than for any one brand.

questions.questionText: A government wishes to encourage young adults to buy their first home, by providing a subsidy to the builder. Which area on the diagram represents the size of the consumer surplus to those who buy a house with such a subsidy? price of S houses 1 $ S VV 2 300 000 Z W 240 000 X YY D O quantity of houses

options.A: V + W + X B V + W + Z C W + X + Y D X + Y + Z

questions.questionText: A government introduces a subsidy for product X and the market price of X falls by 5%. The cross elasticity demand for product Y, with respect to the price of product X, is +0.4. What will happen to the demand for product Y?

options.A: It will decrease by 2%.
options.B: It will decrease by 12.5%.
options.C: It will increase by 2%.
options.D: It will increase by 12.5%.

questions.questionText: Prices of gold, silver and copper fell considerably in 2011 and again in 2015. The fall in prices in 2011 was said to be because miners increased production. The fall in prices in 2015 was because demand, especially from China, decreased. Assuming that the equilibrium before 2011 was X, how would these movements in 2011 and subsequently in 2015 be shown on the demand and supply diagram? price X T Q S R O quantity initial 2011 2015 equilibrium equilibrium equilibrium

options.A: X Q R
options.B: X R Q
options.C: X S R
options.D: X T S

questions.questionText: The price elasticity of supply of a good is elastic. Assuming all production is sold, which combination correctly describes the link between the impact of a rise in price on the quantity supplied and the total revenue received by the firm? quantity supplied rises by total revenue

options.A: greater percentage than price falls
options.B: greater percentage than price rises
options.C: smaller percentage than price falls
options.D: smaller percentage than price rises

questions.questionText: A local government is deciding whether to increase car parking charges and provide more lanes for bus use only. One official said that the increase in car parking charges should cause more bus travel.

options.A: correct correct
options.B: correct incorrect
options.C: incorrect correct
options.D: incorrect incorrect

questions.questionText: What is nationalisation?

options.A: immigrant workers being granted permission to work in a country
options.B: protecting domestic industries from foreign competition
options.C: the government determining which goods should be produced
options.D: transfer of a company from private ownership to government control

questions.questionText: What would be classified by economists as an increase in transfer payments?

options.A: a reallocation of spending from defence to education
options.B: additional funding for government pensions
options.C: extra spending on public sector infrastructure
options.D: increased salaries paid to the police

questions.questionText: A government provided additional free hospital care to its citizens. What happened as a result?

options.A: The supply of merit goods reduced.
options.B: The supply of merit goods increased.
options.C: The supply of private goods reduced.
options.D: The supply of public goods increased.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a market that is currently in equilibrium. S price P P P D O quantity

options.A: All consumers and some producers will lose if OP becomes the minimum price.
options.B: All consumers will be unaffected if OP becomes the maximum price.
options.C: No producers will gain if OP becomes the maximum price.
options.D: All producers will gain if OP becomes the maximum price.

questions.questionText: A government introduces a subsidy to encourage the purchase of electric cars. supply before subsidy price supply after subsidy R S Q T P U demand O W V quantity Which area on the diagram represents the cost to the government?

options.A: OPUV B PQTU C PRSU D QRST

questions.questionText: What would be recorded in the financial account of India’s balance of payments?

options.A: An Indian steel manufacturer buys insurance for its factories from a firm in Europe.
options.B: An Indian steel manufacturer employs foreign workers in its Indian factories.
options.C: An Indian steel manufacturer receives profits from its factories in Europe.
options.D: An Indian steel manufacturer supplies investment for a new factory in Europe.

questions.questionText: Why might an unfavourable movement in a country’s terms of trade benefit its economy?

options.A: It would force inefficient firms out of business.
options.B: It would increase the quantity of goods available for domestic consumption.
options.C: It would make domestically-produced goods more expensive than imports.
options.D: It would make the country’s exports relative to imports more competitive internationally.

questions.questionText: Two industries in a country are fishing and tourism. The foreign exchange rate of the country’s currency fell in 2010. If there were no other changes, how was the country affected?

options.A: Local people bought more imported goods because they were cheaper.
options.B: The price of fish sold in foreign markets became cheaper.
options.C: The volume of exports decreased.
options.D: Tourists to the country were discouraged by higher prices.

questions.questionText: Why might a government wish to increase the value of its foreign exchange rate when the sum of the price elasticity of demand for imports and exports is greater than 1?

options.A: to attract more tourists into the country
options.B: to improve the current account of the balance of payments in the long run
options.C: to increase inflation if the country is in recession
options.D: to make imported raw materials cheaper

questions.questionText: The table shows the levels of a country’s consumer prices index (CPI) between 2015 and 2019. CPI 2015 100 2016 99 2017 98 2018 101 2019 102 Compared with the previous year, in which year was there disinflation but not deflation?

A small country imports tractors. The government of this country decides to impose a quota on imported tractors. What is likely to be the effect on the price of imported tractors and domestic output of tractors? price of domestic output imported tractors of tractors

options.A: fall fall
options.B: increase no change
options.C: no change fall
options.D: no change increase

questions.questionText: What would be likely to increase inflation in an economy?

options.A: an increase in consumer saving
options.B: an increase in interest rates
options.C: an increase in labour productivity
options.D: an increase in taxes on imports

questions.questionText: Japan is suffering from deflation. Which government policy would not help to overcome this problem?

options.A: encouraging domestic savings rather than consumption
options.B: increasing incentives for business start-ups by lowering profits tax
options.C: lowering interest rates and increasing the money supply
options.D: promoting more innovation in technical industries

questions.questionText: A country depreciates its currency to improve the current account of its balance of payments. The effect of the policy is shown. current current account account balance surplus Y +ve time deficit –ve X What is the most likely cause of the movement from X to Y?

options.A: The combined income elasticity of demand for exports and imports is +2.0.
options.B: The combined income elasticity of demand for exports and imports is +0.2.
options.C: The combined price elasticity of demand for exports and imports is –2.0.
options.D: The combined price elasticity of demand for exports and imports is –0.2.

questions.questionText: A country has adopted a fixed exchange rate system but is currently experiencing high unemployment and a deficit in the current account of its balance of payments. Which combination of policies would be most likely to improve both the level of unemployment and the current account of the balance of payments?

options.A: additional net spending by the government and a devaluation of the currency
options.B: additional net spending by the government and revaluation of the currency
options.C: a reduction in net spending by the government and a devaluation of the currency
